A.explanation: Only Bob and Carol are available. With a two-day maximum each, they can cover at most four of five days. Removing availability allows three people to cover five days; removing the per-person limit allows Bob and Carol to cover five days; reducing coverage to four days is also feasible. Therefore the unique minimal conflict set is {availability, coverage, per_person_max}.

2.proof: Two people per day for five days require 10 person-days. Three people working at most two days each provide at most 6, so this case is infeasible.

regression_old_7day.note: This is the earlier flawed instance. Even without availability, coverage and a two-day maximum are infeasible for seven days because 3*2=6<7. Availability was redundant and therefore not part of a minimal conflict set. The current five-day instance makes availability necessary to the minimal conflict set.
